commits.author: clearworks-ai
commits.subject: fix(telegram): only advance poller offset after handlers succeed (#30)
commits.body:
The previous pollOnce implementation advanced `this.offset` to
`update.update_id + 1` before handlers ran and caught handler errors
silently, so any failure in the PTY inject path (or a crash mid-batch)
would leave the update acknowledged to Telegram but never delivered to
the agent. Messages were silently lost.

New semantics:
- The offset advances only after every registered handler for an
  update returns without throwing.
- If a handler throws, the update is left un-acknowledged (Telegram
  re-delivers on the next getUpdates call) and the rest of the batch
  is deferred to preserve ordering.
- The offset is persisted after each successful update, not just at
  the end of the batch, so a crash mid-batch preserves confirmed state.

Adds tests/unit/telegram/poller.test.ts covering: success path,
message-handler throw, mid-batch failure and ordering, per-update
persistence, callback-handler success, and callback-handler throw.

Co-authored-by: Josh Weiss <joshweiss@Joshs-Mac-mini.local>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.body:
* fix(daemon): re-read max_session_seconds on timer fire (BUG-048) + add usage API script

- BUG-048: session timer now re-reads config.json on each check so a
  config change after start() takes effect. Prevents fleet-wide
  simultaneous restarts when max_session_seconds is briefly reduced and
  then restored after timers are already set. Rescheduled if remaining
  time > 5s, fires immediately otherwise.
- bus/check-usage-api.sh: new script to check Claude Max API usage via
  OAuth endpoint with 3-minute cache, threshold alerts via Telegram, and
  --warn-7day / --warn-5h flags.
- 441/441 tests passing (2 new BUG-048 regression tests added).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(daemon): use single quotes in send-telegram instructions to prevent shell variable expansion (BUG-050)

Dollar signs followed by digits (e.g. $100) were stripped from Telegram
messages because the 'Reply using:' instruction templates used double
quotes around <your reply>. Bash expands $100 as ${1}0 (first positional
param + "0"), leaving just the trailing digits.

Fix: change all five formatTelegram* instruction strings from
double quotes to single quotes, matching the existing pattern used for
send-message (line 188). Single-quoted strings are not subject to shell
variable expansion.

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): guard auto-start behind require.main to prevent accidental spawn (#45)
commits.body:
Any require('./dist/daemon.js') (e.g. in a test one-liner) previously started
a full live daemon — IPC server, TelegramPollers, Claude PTY processes — as a
side effect. This caused the double-response incident on 2026-04-12 where a
test command spawned a rogue daemon that ran 31+ minutes alongside the main
daemon, creating duplicate Telegram pollers and persistent conflict errors.

Wrapping the startup block with `require.main === module` makes the module safe
to import/require without side effects while preserving normal execution under
node, PM2, and all existing launch paths.

Closes #44

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(agents-md): single-quote all send-telegram examples to prevent dollar-sign stripping (BUG-052) (#48)
commits.body:
AGENTS.md is the bootstrap file all agents read at session start. Its
send-telegram examples used double quotes, so agents learned to compose
proactive messages (heartbeats, reports, briefings) with double-quoted
shell commands. When the message contained a dollar amount like $1,277,
bash expanded $1 to empty, producing ,277 in the sent message.

BUG-050 (PR #41) fixed the reactive reply template in fast-checker.ts
but missed this upstream teaching pattern. This commit fixes the root
cause: all six send-telegram examples in the template now use single
quotes, matching the pattern agents should use in their own commands.

Per-agent AGENTS.md files in orgs/ are updated separately (not tracked
by git — applied via sed to all 11 agent directories).

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(telegram): add fetch timeout so poller cannot silently hang (#86)
commits.body:
* fix(telegram): add fetch timeout so poller cannot silently hang

Node's built-in fetch has no default timeout. When the TCP connection
to api.telegram.org hangs (NAT rebind, wifi hiccup, ISP buffering) the
await never resolves and never throws. The per-agent Telegram pollers
were silently wedging on this, then dumping the accumulated backlog in
one batch when the socket recovered — observed as "all 9 agents silent
for ~10 minutes, then a burst of replies".

Add AbortSignal.timeout(15000) to post() and AbortSignal.timeout(30000)
to downloadFile(). Surface AbortError/TimeoutError as a clean retryable
"Telegram API request timed out" so the poller's existing catch-and-
continue loop recovers on the next tick (1s pollInterval).

Includes a vitest unit test that mocks a never-resolving fetch and
verifies the abort fires with the expected error message, plus a happy-
path test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(telegram): extend abort timeout to sendPhoto and sendDocument

Reviewer flagged that sendPhoto and sendDocument still used bare fetch()
without AbortSignal, so outbound media could silently hang on the same
wedged-TCP failure mode as the inbound poller. 60s timeout (longer than
post()/getUpdates because uploads can legitimately take longer on slow
links). Same TimeoutError/AbortError mapping to a clean retryable error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
